name: meanrev-selectivity-v1
description: Selectivity/turnover axis for meanrev_stocks — the sleeve's protocol failure mode is not the edge (live 30d: +$2,080, WR 72%, expectancy +$71.74) but TURNOVER (2,550 trades over the long window; Sharpe 0.49 vs SPY 0.79; costs kill it under stress). Pre-registered question: does any point on the SELECTIVITY axis — stricter entryRsi (5 -> 3 -> 2, i.e. rarer/deeper panics) x fewer concurrent slots (maxPositions 5 -> 3) — produce fewer trades with better net-of-costs expectancy, measured by the SAME gates as meanrev-stocks-v1 including minExcessSharpeVsBench (the fair vara for a low-exposure sleeve; NOT relaxed)? The Connors thesis is intact: only the entry threshold and slot count move; smaLong 200, smaExit 5, timeStopDays 10, slotPct 0.1 and the ledger 4% stop are FROZEN to the incumbent (the stop axis is a separate, already-run sweep — mixing axes here would multiply the trial surface). Ranking under scarcity is the engine's own (real MeanRevEngine ranks entries; entryRsi doubles as the quality threshold). A minimum-rank-quality axis beyond entryRsi does NOT exist in the frozen sim params and was deliberately NOT added mid-investigation. 6 candidates = full 3x2 grid, declared BEFORE running; the incumbent (5,5) is meanrev-stocks-v1's incumbent config (0 new hypotheses); the other 5 are new. priorUniqueTrials=18: 9 inventoried pre-manifest experiments + meanrev-stocks-v1's 4 candidates + meanrev-stop-sizing-v1's 5 stop-axis candidates (meanrev-stop-sizing-v2 re-runs those same configs on a longer window and adds 0, per the ledger identity rule). Inventory incomplete, so complete=false and approval stays blocked by protocol regardless of gates. If NO candidate passes, that is the finding — do NOT trim or re-run.
